utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-32-T, the Prosecutor versus Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Witness, when you spoke about the event which preceded the transfer of those people to the house which was burned down, you said that four individuals whom you named arrived and that all four of them had flashlights in their hands; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Could you please explain to us what kind of flashlights they were, the hand-held long ones or the square short ones? Were you able to observe the kind of flashlights they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were carrying military flashlights, round in shape and rather large.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you say they were round, what exactly do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That they were round and not square, as you said. I don't know how you would explain that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Am I to understand that those flashlights were some 10 or 15 centimetres long, where the actual light and battery is behind the bulb?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So they were lighting the area between the two houses with those flashlights?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And Memic house, where you were on that night, did have lights on; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: However, the house which you indicated as being the house where people, including yourself, were eventually taken to, the Omeragic house, was not lit at all except for the light coming from those flashlights; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On that night, the house -- that house was not lit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember the room in question, in particular the door of that room? Was there any door, and if "yes," what kind of door was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a door. However, I was unable to observe what kind of door it was because of the dark. I didn't pay much attention to the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You approximated for us. You said that the room was eight by eight metres large. Were you able to have a good look at the room and be certain as to its size?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you gave the description of your escape from that room and you told us that you had jumped out of the second window, do you remember whether anyone else had jumped out before you, or were you the first person to have jumped out of the window, if you can remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. VG18 had jumped out before me. Then I did. And after me, VG048.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: As far as I understood, after you had jumped out of the window, you no longer saw any of those individuals anywhere near the house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So how is it that you know that that individual jumped out of you [sic]? Is it because she managed to save herself, or is it because she survived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I jumped out of the window, sir, I did linger around a little bit, and I managed to see VG084 jumping out of the window after me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, it may be a typographical error, but his earlier answer was that VG84 jumped out after him, and then after him, VG48. Now there's no 48 on these lists, but there is an 84 on these lists. I assume that's the same person.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. First time he said 48, and after that he said 84. I think that is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It's not a typographical error, but it may be that we better know who he means by "VG48."

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, have you heard the question? Could you please explain to us whether you misspoke when you identified the witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may have been my mistake. 084.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you remember when it was that you first learned about the arrest of Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember, but I remember reading about it in the paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you say "in the paper," I assume you are referring to the newspaper which was published in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember by any chance what paper it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in Oslobodenje.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Were there any photographs in that article, his photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: In the meantime, that is, in the period of time after his arrest and afterwards, did you watch or hear anything about him and his proceedings either on TV or in the papers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I regularly followed that subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So in the "Hague Chronicle" he was shown as being here in the courtroom, in the Hague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You gave a statement to the investigator of the Office of the Prosecutor several years ago; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yesterday, you were shown a photo spread on which you signed your name under the photograph of the individual whom you said was Mitar Vasiljevic, and you also wrote down the date when you identified him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: However, you did not do that -- you did not identify him on the first occasion when you gave the statement to the investigator. Were you also shown his photograph on that first occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was shown his photograph at the time of my interview, before I read the papers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Let me be specific. On the first occasion when you gave an interview to the Office of the Prosecutor here in the Hague - I'm referring to your first statement - were you given an opportunity on that particular occasion to identify and recognise Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember when it was that you recognised Mitar Vasiljevic in the photo spread?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I recognised him immediately on those photographs, which included his photograph as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, but my question referred to the time when that took place. When was it that you were shown that particular photo spread -- or let me be more specific. Was that on the 21st of June, 2001, this year? If necessary, perhaps you could have another look at the photo spread.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in the month of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: The month of June of this year, 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me ask you a few questions concerning your first statement given to the Office of the Prosecutor, the one which you gave before the arrest of Mitar Vasiljevic. You stated in that statement, among other things, that before your arrival in Visegrad, you were first put up in a house near the old hotel, that it was there that you spent the night, and that you went to Jusuf Memic's house in the Nova Mahala neighbourhood only the following day. You also stated that the individual whom you identified as Mitar escorted you to the house and that the event took place around 3.00, 3.00 p.m., then on the second day that you spent one night -- that is, that you spent one night in a house near the old hotel. Do you remember stating that to the investigator?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Perhaps what is not correct is the fact that you had spent one night there before that, but I'm asking you whether that was what you stated to the -- in the statement given to the investigator of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I never mentioned any house near a hotel, nor that we spent the night there, but that we stayed in the Nova Mahala neighbourhood in the house belonging to Jusuf Memic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Let me read you the statement. Let me quote that perhaps to refresh your memory. "First we stayed in a house close to an old hotel. From there, three men were taken out to bury dead people. The three men were Alija Kurspahic, Becar Kurspahic, and Redzo Memisevic. They are all dead now. They did not tell us the names of the people they buried. The next day, we were told by Mitar Vasiljevic to go to the house of Jusuf Memic, also in Mahala. Mitar escorted us to the house. This happened around 3.00." Do you remember having stated that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those people went to bury the dead, but we were staying in Jusuf Memic's house at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: However, that is not what you stated in respect of those individuals. I asked you yesterday specifically if any people were taken out and then taken back to that particular house, and you said, "No."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because I couldn't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: The fact that you cannot remember, is it perhaps because at the time you were 13 and a half?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness. This concludes my cross-examination, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Re-examination, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yesterday, Mr. Domazet asked you about your observations of Mitar Vasiljevic with Mr. (redacted). Do you recall your testimony on that matter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: During the time that you made your observations of this, did you at any time see Mr. (redacted) leave the house or leave the area and return?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was standing there with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That was my next question. At any time, did you see these two men sitting, or were they always standing at the time you observed them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were standing there all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And approximately how long were they together in total?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you the exact time, but I know that they were standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you give us your best estimate of the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For about 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you testified regarding your observations of Mr. Susnjar by the house, the Omeragic house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You testified regarding your ability or -- your observations of Mr. Susnjar when he threw a grenade or threw a bomb into the window of the Omeragic house. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was the lighting sufficient at that period of time to see Mr. Susnjar clearly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was the fire, not the lighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Domazet asked you about several opportunities you may have had to see either pictures or photographs or video of Mr. Vasiljevic in the news media, and my question to you is: When you saw these pictures, did you immediately recognise the person who you saw in these photographs and news media as Mr. Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recognised him immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And your identification of Mr. Vasiljevic in the group of photos that you were shown, was that based on seeing Mr. Vasiljevic in the news media, or was it based on your observations of him back in the spring of '92?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG38 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of my recollections from 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you, sir, for coming along to give evidence. We're very grateful to you for coming and for the evidence you've given. You are now free to leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution calls VG13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. It will be Exhibit P89, and it is under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, madam, would you please make the solemn declaration in the form of the document which the usher is showing you. Would you read it out, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would ask that we begin by showing the witness P89.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Good morning, VG13.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The document entitled "P89" has just been placed before you. I would ask you to read the top line of that document and ask you: Is that your name at the top?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Read it to herself.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sorry. Read it to yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is that your name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And on the second line, I'd ask you to read to yourself what's written there and ask you: Is that your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: For the purposes of concealing your identity, we will refer to you as "VG13" throughout these proceedings. If you need to refer to any of the people listed on that sheet, I would ask you to do so by referring to their number below.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us where you were born?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: In Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And for most of your life, have you lived in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And are you married?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And do you have children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Three children.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And is one of those children VG38 on your sheet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us how far you attended or how many grades of school you attended?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Four grades of primary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was that in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: As an adult, did you work in a company in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us what village you're from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: I was born in the village of [redacted], and my husband is from the village of Koritnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What village did you live in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: In [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What is your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: I am Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: In 1992, were you a member of any political party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And your husband?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: He wasn't ever a member either.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to draw your attention now to the 10th of June, 1992. Do you recall that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes, I remember it well, when our village was attacked.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Who attacked your village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Chamber what occurred.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: They attacked us. They wanted us to give them weapons. They were looking for men and such like.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you actually speak to these people who attacked you, or did you have a face-to-face confrontation with these people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Who were these people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: There was Milovan Jasika, Miloje Gavrilovic, Dusan Grujic, Ljubisa Grujic, Mladjo Grujic, Radomir Djuric, Gavrilovic, and others. I didn't see them all, but these I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: As a result of this attack, did you have to move from the house that you were living in at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: I did. I wasn't -- I was a bit outside the village, so I had to go to the Kurspahic house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you do that because you believed you would be safer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: We weren't safe anywhere, but we went there to be together.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened to the young men in the village at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: At that time, well, there was shooting -- or rather, as soon as there was a lull in the shooting, some boys crossed the fields and went into the woods, whereas the older men stayed in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: After this attacks, did you have an opportunity to go outside and see evidence of the attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: We went outside, and Ilija Gavrilovic came in front of the door of Sumbula Kurspahic's looking for her son and the other men.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know what village Ilija Gavrilovic came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Also from the village of Koritnik, one village next to another.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: In civilian clothes. He had two pistols on him, and he held one in his hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was he alone or with other people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: There was Radomir Djuric from the neighbouring village of Loznica. And his nickname is "Cinda". That's how they call him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was there anyone else aside from these two men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: There were others in the village, but I didn't really look around. There was fear. There was chaos.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At that time, were you able to see any damage to the houses caused by this attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: There was some damage from bullets and some kind of shells. I don't know how I can explain. Those that you shoot from the shoulder with a tube like this. So I really don't know much about weapons, but that's what they looked like.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately how long were those men there at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: The men that attacked us?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: They stayed for about an hour looking for weapons. The men, they found an old man, Osman Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did they do anything to Mr. Kurspahic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: They didn't do anything to him at the time, but they just told him to find his rifle and surrender it, and his son.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time two or three days that these men returned to the village of Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: They never came back to the village again. They didn't dare come back.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when soldiers came back and surrounded the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: They came looking again, but we were hiding in the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you were told that you had to leave the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes, Dusan Grujic told us and Milorad Lipovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Well, that was the 13th -- between the 13th and the 14th they told us we had to move out.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And Dusan Grujic, where was he from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Also from the village of Koritnik. (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I ask you to tell us, using the words that Mr. Grujic used himself, what exactly did he say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic said to us that we should pack some food for one day and one set of clothing because we had to leave the village because there was ethnic cleansing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did he tell you where you were going to be taken to, or where you would go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: He said that we would go to Kladanj, to be exchanged and that Serbs would come to live in our houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did he say when you would have to leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: On the 14th, we left our village. That is what we were told to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: On the 13th, the night of the 13th, did you pack some things to take with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes, we packed some things.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What kinds of things did you pack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: A change of clothing and food that would be sufficient for a day or two.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you take any other personal possessions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: I took my documents, some money, and such like.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you think that you would be returning to your home in (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Well, yes. We thought that after a short while, we would go back; however, we didn't go back.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe for us what happened on the morning of the 14th.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: On the 14th, in the morning, we got ready. It was raining. And our neighbours told us nicely that the bus would come. But that was a trick. The bus didn't come. About half past 8.00, our neighbours came to plunder our village before our eyes. They loaded whatever they wanted and took away. They took away our tractors and everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you see this yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Personally I saw this, and I stand by whatever I am saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What was the ethnicity of the neighbours that you say plundered your possessions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When the bus did not come, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Our neighbour Grujic and Milorad Lipovac told us to go on on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: This Grujic that you are referring to now, is this the same person you referred to earlier as Dusan Grujic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you go towards Visegrad on foot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: We did. We reached Greben. We moved slowly because there were old people and small children, and then two soldiers came up. I didn't recognise them. I didn't dare look. One had a beard. And they asked us where we were going, and mistreated us, and beat us, and they wanted to kill us. And then his colleague said, "Don't do anything now. We'll go to Prelevo, and then when we come back, we see."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did any of -- did either Mr. Lipovac or Mr. Grujic accompany you on your trip towards Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Dusan accompanied us as far as [sic] Milorad Lipovac, and then he told him you take over and leave them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What village was that that occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: The village of Greben.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you reached the intersection of the road between Greben and Visegrad and the road that leads up to the Vilina Vlas Hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did something happen in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: There, again, they stopped us and said that the buses would come there. And they were discussing the possibility of killing us there next to the Drina River.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did Mr. Lipovac say anything at this time regarding the possibility of you being killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Mr. Lipovac said to these men, "Don't kill them here," and take them to the town - and I apologise - that they should fuck us as they want.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you familiar with a young woman by the name of "Jasmina Vila"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: From the village of Musici. She's a neighbour. It's also a neighbouring village.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was she with you that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: She was with us, and Stanislava Susnjar brought her, because Milan Lukic had brought her from the village of Kamenica, from the hunting lodge. She looked awful, and then she went on with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe her condition in greater detail, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: She was black here. She had bruises and cuts. Her hair was all untidy. She looked awful. There were bites, traces of bites. Her face was peeling from these bites.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where did she join the group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Stanislava Susnjar brought her to our village because they are close by. She said, "We can't keep her here." She brought her on the 13th, and "As you're going the next morning," she said, "let her go with you."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately how many people altogether were in the group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: About 70, including those from Sase and us from our village, so about 75.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did there come a time when this group eventually did reach the centre of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: We arrived about 3.00 or 4.00 in the afternoon, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where did this journey end, what part of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: The journey ended when we reached Janidja [phoen], it's called, the Red Cross. But it was Sunday, nothing was working, so we went in front of the new hotel, in the terrace of the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Why did you go to the Red Cross building or Red Cross office?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: That's what they told us, because the Red Cross was allegedly going to take us over.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And when you say "they," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: People in the Red Cross who were working there. Milorad Lipovac and these others told us, "You would be registered there and then you'll go on from there."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did those two men themselves tell you they were working for the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: They didn't say they were working for the Red Cross, but they just gave us those instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Chamber, where is the Red Cross office in relation to the place you've described as "the new hotel"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: It comes first, before the new hotel, and apparently that was where the Red Cross -- but it wasn't there. Before the hotel, on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask you to describe the area in front of the hotel. Can you describe for us the area in which this group gathered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: There's a street, the street where we had gathered, and we got -- we assembled in front of the new hotel, the terrace of the hotel, all of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Aside from the group of people from Koritnik and Sase, what other people were on the street at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: We met people in the street, but I didn't take note of who they were. There were there people walking around.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you see any people in uniforms at that time on the street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes, we did. We saw there police, and there were soldiers too around.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe the uniforms that the police were wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: The police wore blue uniforms with badges on their sleeves and caps, some kind of little flags.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did the uniforms appear to be the same uniform that the police wore before the conflict began?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: No. These were darker than the old ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could you see the insignia on these uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: I did. I saw these small flags on their caps and on their sleeves.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was that different from the insignias that the police wore before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did any of these police say anything to the group of people from Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: They mistreated us, and he said, "These should be killed straight away right here."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know the name of that person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: I don't know his name, but he did abuse us and asked us, "Where are your men? They've gone to join the Green Berets," and he cussed us like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you approximate for us how many police were present during the time you were in front of the new hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: There were three. They came to meet us. Then I saw others. But I didn't really look around. I was so scared, I didn't even dare look at myself, never mind around.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You mentioned earlier in your testimony that soldiers were present as well. Can you tell us approximately how many soldiers were present, if you're able?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: I didn't count them, but there were some.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you describe how they were dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: They were wearing camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were the police armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: They were armed too, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How long did you remain in this area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: We stayed for about an hour, maybe longer, until they told us to go to Pionirska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And who did you tell -- or who told you to go to Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Brana Tesovic walked in. He was a waiter and he was a worker at Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Hidrogradnja. And he said to one of our colleagues that in order to avoid being mistreated, that we should go to Pionirska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you and the group leave for Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes, we did, we headed in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did anybody accompany the group up to Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: We were followed by some people, but I didn't turn around to look and see who they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: They were people that were not with the group from Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to tell whether the people that followed you were armed or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: They were armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were you able to tell whether they were -- had some type of uniform on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: As I turned around once, I saw that policemen were following us, but I didn't turn back again.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How long did it take the group to reach or to go from the new hotel to Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: We went slowly. It took us about half an hour, maybe a little longer, because it was raining and there were elderly with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you reached Pionirska Street, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: One group went to Jusuf Memic's house, and the others went to Mujo Memic's house. Mujo was Jusuf's son.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were these houses next to each other?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Which house did you go to initially?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Mujo Memic's.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And approximately how many people out of the group went to Mujo Memic's house initially?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: About four families.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the remainder of the group went to Jusuf Memic's house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: After you were inside of Mujo Memic's house, did anybody come to the door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: After we had a cup of coffee and we changed our clothes because we were wet, Mr. Mitar came. He gave Mujo a piece of paper, some sort of certificate that we should not be afraid of anything, that we would be quite safe.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The person you're referring to as "Mitar," do you know this person's last name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you describe for the Court how you knew this person's name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: I knew Mr. Mitar as a waiter in the Panos Hotel, and sometimes he would be working at the new hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us, for what period of time did you know Mr. Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: I knew him quite a long time, even when he was a young man. We would go to get-togethers, parties, and he went to school with a relative of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe what he was wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: He was wearing a black suit and a black hat at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were you able to tell if he was armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: He came to give (redacted) the certificate, and he didn't have a weapon. He was not armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time, in connection with this case, that an investigator from the Office of the Prosecutor showed you a group of photos of different men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: No, they didn't show me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you ever recall being shown photographs of different people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was that by an investigator of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that the witness be shown --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: -- witness be shown Prosecution Number 55-VG13, already admitted into evidence. And I'm going to ask the witness to look at both the front and the back of that exhibit. I would ask you to look at both the front and the reverse of those documents in front of you. Do you recognise that group of photos, VG13?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you shown those photographs on an earlier occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Not until now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I would ask you to turn over to the reverse of Exhibit 55-VG13. Can you look at the rear of the page. Do you recognise any of the signatures on that page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Without saying any of the names, is your signature on that page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you recall now whether you were shown these photographs at an earlier point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Out of these ten pictures of men, did you recognise one of the people among them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Who did you recognise that person to be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what number is next to his picture?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Four.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm going to ask you to look around the courtroom this morning and ask you if you recognise anybody in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: I can recognise Mitar, my neighbour, the gentleman over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe where he is sitting and what he is wearing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: He is sitting on the left side. He is wearing a brown suit and an off-white shirt.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't want to repeat my mistake of yesterday. Using the words the record reflects, may we mark this for identification somehow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It will be noted that the witness has identified the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The first time that you saw Mr. Vasiljevic at the house of Mujo Memic, did he say anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: The first time he came, he brought the certificate and he told us to gather near Memic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At that time that you saw him, was he alone or with somebody else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: At that time, he was alone, standing in front of the door, whereas we were inside the house. But then we went to the other house, the adjacent house, and then he left.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Why did you go to the other house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Well, we didn't know why we had to go there. They had probably organised themselves in advance. They probably knew why they were gathering us there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did somebody tell you to move from the house of Mujo Memic to the house of Jusuf Memic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes. At about 10.00 or 10.30, they took our gold and our money. They told us to take off our clothes, and they mistreated us and beat us. And after that, they told us to go to Memic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Before we talk about that --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Sorry, the Omeragic house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I would like to ask you a few questions about this paper you referred to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us exactly -- let me ask you this: Did you actually see this piece of paper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes. Mujo showed it to us, and I was standing next to him. We were all there together. And written on that piece of paper was "Do not be afraid. Nobody is going to harm you". And Mr. Vasiljevic, my neighbour, he explicitly told us that the following morning, we would be taken over by the Red Cross. And everything had been prepared in advance. They knew what they would do with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I ask you to tell us, using the words that Mr. Vasiljevic used, exactly what he said regarding the Red Cross at that time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: I don't know why he said that. Probably to comfort us a little bit, to reassure us so that we wouldn't be afraid. But we were already afraid when we left that house -- when we left our houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to see a signature on that piece of paper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: I could see everything, the way I can see this paper in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was there a signature on that paper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes, there was a signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to tell whose signature it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Well, it was his signature, since he was the one who brought the paper, and he wrote it down. As soon as you write something down, you have to sign it so as to make it yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I would ask you, just so we're clear, who is -- who are you referring to? Who is the "he" whose signature is on this paper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Mr. Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time after this that some of the men in the group from Koritnik were taken away to do some work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately what time of the day did this happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Well, when we got there, in the early evening hours, Alija Kurspahic left together with Medo to bury a man who had been killed, together with his wife. He used to work at the veterinarian station. I don't know what their surname is. They went to bury him. And when they came back, we were told that he and his wife had been killed, and that they had to go there to bury them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you see the people who came to take these men away to do this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: This police force of theirs went there to pick them up, I suppose, but somebody must have brought them where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You did not see that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: I could see. But frankly, I'm not able to tell you who it was. It was Mitar who came to take them over there to bury those people.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Again, I would ask you to just say the last name of the person you are referring to as "Mitar."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you approximate for us what time this occurred at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: I did not have a watch. Nobody had a watch. The watches had been seized from us. But I think that it was about 5.00, 5.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe what Mr. Vasiljevic was wearing at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: The same black suit and black hat.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time later in the day when you saw Mr. Vasiljevic again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was he alone or in the company of other people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Milan Lukic, Bosko Djuric, Milan Susnjar were there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was there just those four men, or were there others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: There were probably others as well, but I didn't dare watch. I didn't dare count them. We were afraid. We hardly knew where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you, yourself, see any other people aside from these four that you have mentioned by name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Of course. There were people walking around the Nova Mahala neighbourhood, and the residents were being gathered on Pionirska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The person you refer to as Milan Lukic, can you tell the Court how it is you came to learn his name or how do you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: I know Milan Lukic just as I know Mitar Vasiljevic. They all come from neighbouring villages. He is from Rujiste, and there were Serb villages, Muslim villages, and mixed villages in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you approximate for us how long it is that you know or knew Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Well, I had known him for quite some time, like I had known Mr. Mitar Vasiljevic and others. I lived in that town, so I knew all my neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The person you referred to as Milan Susnjar, can you tell us how it was you knew him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And Mr. Bosko Djuric who you mentioned, how did you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: He is also from a neighbouring village, the village of Loznica.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What occurred after these men arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: What occurred was that our money and gold were taken away from us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Will you tell us specifically what happened, how did that occur.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Milan Lukic came to the house, and he threw a piece of cloth onto a table, and he told us to assemble, to sit down, to get together in one room. He said, "You should put all your jewellery and money here, everything that you have. If you do not surrender everything that you have, you will get a bullet in your forehead, and you will be searched once again." We gave them everything we had. And after they had taken all our belongings, they sent us to another room, to a next-door room, and told us to take off our clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: In which house is this occurring?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: In Jusuf Memic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And this other room that you're referring to, can you describe what room it was in the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: We were in the kitchen, which is in the left-hand side. And on the right-hand side, there were two rooms. And in one of the rooms, we were made to take off our clothes. We had to do it, and they made us dance around.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what was the purpose of making you dance around or the people in the group dance around?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Well, all of us women who had taken our clothes off had to dance individually around Mr. Milan Susnjar. And the others were standing around the house, guarding the house so that we wouldn't jump out.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened to young children that were there at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Well, we also had to take their clothes off so that they could check that nobody had hidden anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was there one young woman who refused to take her clothes off?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes. So other women were made to take her clothes off.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately how long did this take?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: It took about two hours, the dancing, they mistreating us, telling us what to do, how to dance, how to turn around.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was your watch taken at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes, everything. We had to take off our earrings, everything. We had to give them everything we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were watches taken from the other people in the group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Everything. We gave them everything. Though he may have thrown it away and not used it at all, it's just that everything was taken from us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when two women in the house were actually taken out of the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And do you know the name of those two women?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Ifeta Kurspahic, Jasmina, and Mujesira Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So there were three women taken out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The person you referred to as "Jasmina," what is her last name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: "Vila."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And is this the same "Jasmina Vila" who you referred to earlier in your testimony as coming from the village of Uzice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe the circumstances under which these women were taken out of the house of Jusuf Memic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: The girls were taken out, and when they returned, they didn't look quite in shape. Jasmina wanted me to give her a tablet. And we asked them what had happened, and they said, "Well, you know what happened." They didn't want to tell anything. And Ifeta, when she came back, she also looked bad, she was crying, and she said, "Your turn will also come."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What did you understand her to mean by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Well, they managed to tell us that they had been raped, and we could see for ourselves, you know, how they looked after they had been mistreated. And she told -- they told -- they told us to try and escape, because apparently Milan Lukic and others told them that we would all be raped.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you describe the condition of the clothes of these three women?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Well, they were dressed. They were wearing skirts or suits. They were neatly dressed because they had set out on a journey. They were wearing their regular civilian clothes, costumes --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what was the --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: -- and scarves.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What was the condition of their clothes when they returned and spoke with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: They looked dishevelled. Their buttons had been torn off.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to tell whether these women were taken simply to another part of the house or were they taken away from the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: They were taken out of the house. And after about an hour, an hour and a half, they were taken back.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were you able to tell who it was that took these women from the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Milan Lukic took them away. I don't know what happened afterwards. But whatever happened, they came back looking dishevelled, their clothes torn, traces of bites on their skin. They looked as if they had been mistreated.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, at the time that Milan Lukic took them away, were you able to see where the other men that came with Milan Lukic were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: They were around the house. We could see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And approximately what time, if you're able to tell us, did these women return?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: They returned at about 8.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time after this that you became aware that Mitar Vasiljevic and Milan Lukic and the other people you've referred to were no longer present at the Jusuf Memic house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: They were standing around the house, and by the time the girls came back, they no longer entered the house. It was only some time later that they came to take us from Memic's house to Adem Omeragic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And approximately how much time transpired between the time that these young women were returned and the time you were taken to Adem Omeragic's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: From 8.00 up until half past 9.00, 10.00, when they came and knocked on the door. And they told us to get our belongings, to pack and move out, that the place was no longer safe.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you tell us, who returned at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Mitar Vasiljevic, Milan Lukic returned. I could see the two of them at the door. Lukic was holding the door, the knob of the house on Jusuf Memic's house, and he told us to hurry up before the shooting would start. And Mr. Vasiljevic was standing on Adem Omeragic's house, and he was yelling, "Hurry up, hurry up."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did Mr. Lukic say anything regarding who was doing the shooting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Well, he said that our army was shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, aside from Milan Lukic and Mitar Vasiljevic, did you see any other men present at the Jusuf Memic house or in the vicinity of it at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Around the house, there were other people as well, probably their soldiers. But I didn't recognise them because the lighting was not very good. It was further down, so we couldn't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At the time you see Milan Lukic this time, is he armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And does he have anything else with him at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: He had a multicoloured uniform. He was holding a rifle in one hand and holding the door with his other hand, and he told us to hurry up, that there was no time to wait. Kada Sehic asked him for permission to put on her shoes, and he said, "Hurry up. You will need no shoes." And there was one man from our group who asked her, "How do you know it is Lukic," and she said, "He had taken my son away," and her husband, and their names were Rasim and Kender.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And Mr. Vasiljevic at this time, could you tell whether he was armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: At the time, Mr. Vasiljevic was carrying a flashlight.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And aside from the flashlight, did you see whether he was carrying anything else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: He also had a rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe for us precisely where it was -- where it was Mr. Vasiljevic was standing this time that you see him in relation to Jusuf Memic's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: When we left Memic's house, Milan Lukic was holding the door of that house, Jusuf Memic's house. And Mr. Mitar was walking ahead of us, and he brought the first group of people to this other house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And do you know the owner of that other house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes, I know. Amir Omeragic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And are you familiar with a creek in the area of Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes, there is a creek there. It is a kind of derivation for rains, for heavy rains. And there is also a sewage further down.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where is the house of Adem Omeragic in relation to the creek?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Near the creek, some 50 metres -- 10 metres away from the creek.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you've testified that Mr. Vasiljevic was in front of you as you went down to this house. Did there come a point in time when you passed by him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you tell us where that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: While he was holding the door of Adem Omeragic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you walk past him to get inside that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes, we did, because Mitar Vasiljevic was shouting, telling us to hurry up.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did he have a flashlight with him at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Based on your prior knowledge or experience with Mr. Vasiljevic, are you able to recognise his voice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Who is -- what members of your immediate family were with you at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: My son, my mother-in-law, and some other relatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did anything happen to your mother-in-law as she passed Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes. As she was going through the door, and she was an elderly woman, aged over 80. He pushed her and told her to hurry up, and she said, "Why are you pushing me?" And then he cursed her mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At the time that you passed Mr. Vasilejic, can you approximate for us how far is your face from his face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Less than half a metre. It was a passage like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was there anything covering his face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: No. He had a hat, of course, but the lighting was good, and I could see him very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you now to describe the room that you were placed in in the Omeragic house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: The room had a couch inside and a closet, and there were some carpets on the floor, which had been sprayed by something, some product which made the whole atmosphere very suffocating, and it looked like some kind of glue. And we all entered that room, and there were some people who had already been brought there. I don't know who they were. I could only recognise Jasmina who was married to Ahmed Belic, and she was there with her son, who was two years old. Her mother-in-law was also there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately how many people were in that room aside from the people from Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't count them. But as far as I could see, given the kind of lighting that there was, there were some ten people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At this point in time, did you have your shoes on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes, I had the traditional peasant shoes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to tell whether or not the floor was wet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was the floor wet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes, the carpets were wet, because something had been sprinkled over them. I don't know what it was. I know that we were suffocating, but I don't know exactly what kind of product it was. I cannot describe it for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Had you ever smelled anything like that before in your life, or something similar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: No. No, I had not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I suggest we pause there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well. We'll adjourn now until 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Witness 13, when we took the break, you were describing some of the features of the room in the Omeragic house. I want to ask you, were there any lights on in the house at the time you were in it this evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes, there was some light coming from the other side, the other side of the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, this light, was this inside the house or outside the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Outside the house. There was street lighting, and this light reached us, so you could see after all.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was this light that you are referring to now, was it from Pionirska Street or another street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: The name of the street was Glavica, the settlement of Glavica, the neighbourhood of Glavica from where the light was coming.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe where that is in relation to the creek that you've talked about earlier today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: To the left of Adem Omeragic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you approximate for us how far away this street is from the Omeragic house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was about a hundred metres or less, because there was a whole settlement there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were there any lights inside the room that you were in at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: There was no light in the room but only coming from the street lighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you've described a strong smell and suffocating from this smell, earlier today. What did you do in response to that smell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Because of this strong smell, which was unpleasant, with my child, I went up to the window stepping on people's legs, pushing my way through to get some fresh air.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How many windows were in the house that you can recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: I remember well that there were two windows.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And when you refer to your child, are you referring to VG38?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when the entire group from Koritnik was in that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: All of us who were together were in those rooms, except for the people who had got there before us. They were forced there. I don't know how to put it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you estimate for us approximately in total what was the number of people in that room.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: All of us that were there from the village of (redacted), those who joined us from Sase, there were between 70 and 75, plus the people that were already there in Adem Omeragic's room. I didn't count them, but there were ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you complete your answer? The last thing that was interpreted was: "I didn't count them, but there were ..."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: About ten were there for sure, because they were sitting on the sofa. So judging by the light, there were about ten, maybe even more of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, after all the people were inside this room, was the door closed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you describe for us what happened after the door to this room was closed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: When the door was closed, the people started crying. Mr. Mitar Vasiljevic left and we stayed in the house, so that people were crying, shouting, saying, "Pray to God." We awaited what destiny would bring.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And how long did you wait?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: An hour, maybe an hour and a half. I don't know whether it was that much. And then they came again.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe for us what happened when they came again? And I'd ask you to begin by telling us who came again.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Mitar Vasiljevic, Milan Lukic. I saw them when they opened the door. And he held in his hand -- that is, Milan Lukic held some sort of a device. He said, "Light it and put it down next to the door." And this exploded, and immediately the carpets caught fire and the flames started rising.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: When the room was set on fire, two people jumped out of the window. I thought it was someone else, but in fact it was a witness. She will come here and tell you. I don't want to name her. Then another person followed, another witness who was here. They were shooting. They left from below the window. Mitar Vasiljevic came with a flashlight, lighting up the window, and Milan Lukic was shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just going to ask, would the usher please open up the pseudonym sheet on the desk for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to take you back to the time when you referred to the door being opened. I'd ask you to describe what you observed at that time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: When the door opened, I noticed again that this device had been lighted and put down on the ground next to the floor -- next to the door on the inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And who was holding this device?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you describe this device for us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: It's like this, roughly this size, with a kind of fuse on top. And it was burning, and he put it down.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Had you ever seen a device like this before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: No, I hadn't seen it, but -- but I reckon it was a kind of bomb.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And who, if anyone, was with Milan Lukic at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: There was Mitar Vasiljevic. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Anyone else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Well, Bosko Djuric, most probably he was there too. But just then, it was Milan Lukic and Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where was Mitar Vasiljevic in relation to the door of the Omeragic house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Just then, both of them were at the door. But when VG18 jumped out of the window and VG84, at that moment they went underneath the windows of the Omeragic house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to ask you a few more questions about what happened at the door before we move to that portion of your testimony. Can you describe for us in detail what you observed Mitar Vasiljevic do at the time you saw him by the open door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: He was lighting the place with a flashlight.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to tell if he was armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes, he did have.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And do you recall what position -- are you able to tell us what he was armed with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: They were short, small rifles, short butts.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And do you recall the manner in which he was holding that rifle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: In his hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And in which direction was it pointed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: He was holding his rifle in his hand, pointed towards the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At this time, were you able to see Milan Lukic's face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was there anything obstructing your view of his face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to see Mitar Vasiljevic's face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was there anything obstructing your view of his face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was there sufficient light at that time to see his face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Well, I could see well. There was light from the street lamp, and I could see well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you hear -- this device that was lit and placed on the floor. Did you hear it explode?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Well, at that same moment, the rooms started burning, the carpets were in flames, the people were crying. I was next to the window.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you hear an explosion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How much time, can you tell us, transpired between the time that Milan Lukic lit this device and -- I'm sorry. How much time transpired between the time this device was lit and the time you heard an explosion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: I don't know whether it could have been a minute, maybe less, before it exploded.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And you described the carpet catching fire. Did the entire carpet catch fire or only part of it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes, all of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The people that were in the room at this time, would you characterise them as being crowded together, or not crowded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, it was crowded, because the room was small, and there were a lot of us, so that I could hardly reach the window to be able to jump out.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, the flames that came from the carpet, can you describe for us the height of those flames. Using a part of the body as a reference, how high did they come?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: It was so big a flame that it reached the ceiling of that room.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did people's clothes catch fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you've described Witness VG18 and VG84 going out the window of the house. Can you describe for us in greater detail which window of the house you saw that -- them jump from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: The left window, the one I jumped out of following them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where would that window be in relation to the door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: From the door, to the left of the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would it be the window that is closest to the door or furthest from the door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: It was a bit away from the door, but not much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Who went out of the window first?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: VG18 and VG84.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you see anybody else go out of the window at that point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What did you observe after they jumped out of the window?
