utterances.text: Do you remember when you arrived in Medzedza? Would it be some time at the end of July, judging by what you have told us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Well, yes, July, beginning of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was there any other fire in Visegrad? Did you notice any other fire in Visegrad while you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes, at Bikavac, where a house burned down in which there were about perhaps 80 people, and one witness survived. I don't know where he is, and I wouldn't name him anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: My question was whether you saw that fire. Were you still in Visegrad when that happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes. I was in the sewage canal when this happened at Bikavac. And in that canal the stench was choking me from those people. And when I and the survivor met in Medzedza, we had a short talk, because she couldn't speak, and she told me how it all happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: May I take it that this was a few days after what happened in the house of Omeragic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: As I had this encounter with this person, so this was the following night after our experience.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So -- no. Two nights after the Omeragic fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Madam, did you know the individual by the name of "Susnjar" well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Milan Susnjar, yes, [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: During that period of time, did he have a beard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: When he came to take -- to make us take our clothes off, he did not have a beard. As for before that, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did he have a moustache, by any chance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes, he did have a moustache, a black moustache. And he was dark, of medium height.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was that the individual whom you saw on that night in Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you described Mitar Vasiljevic, you said that he was wearing a black suit and a black hat; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember what kind of footwear he had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: He was barefoot when he came to us, and he had some ribbons on his hat.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you saw him on the first occasion, he was barefoot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: When he came, I didn't pay much attention. But then he came barefoot.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: That evening, were you still able to observe that he was barefoot or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: You mean when they marched us from one house to another? No, I didn't pay attention to his feet. I couldn't see whether he was barefoot. But I know that he was wearing a hat, as before, as this time before.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You said you knew Sredoje Lukic very well. You did not mention him, although you mentioned him in your prior statement 16 times. In response to one of my questions, you said that he also took part in these events. Because of a very important fact concerning Mitar's involvement in the events, I have to ask you once again whether at the time this group arrived, the group who looted and took away the young women, did Mitar Vasiljevic leave before that? Did he leave before their arrival?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Now you want me to say that Mitar wasn't there at all?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: All I want to do is to remove certain doubt as to his presence there, because you stated something different in your statement given to the investigator. I have to ask you whether you remember that you stated in the statement to the investigator that Mitar had already left and that it was after his departure that Sredoje Lukic arrived, and then you went on to give their description --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Mitar Vasiljevic left after he had given the certificate to (redacted) (redacted). And during the plunder and the mistreatment, they were all there again.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, but you did not state that in your statement to the investigator. Or do you wish to have a look at the statement? Do you remember? Do you remember having stated there that only Milan and Sredoje Lukic took you from the Memic house to the Omeragic house, where they locked you up, and after which you said disappeared?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: But could you then explain to me who it was who was holding the flashlight when Milan Lukic was shooting at those who were jumping out of the window? I didn't see Sredoje carrying a flashlight. It was Mr. Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, it is true that is what you stated in your statement given to the investigator, that he was holding a flashlight while you were jumping out of the window. However, half an hour before that, you mentioned only the two other individuals. Do you agree with me that you stated in your statement to the investigator that it was Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic who locked you up in that room and left you there, and it was only after that they came again together with Mitar, who was holding a flashlight?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: That Sredoje Lukic was the one who took us to Omeragic house? No, no, because I personally saw Mitar Vasiljevic standing at the door. He was not far from me, the way you are now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Madam, speaking of the lighting, you said that the area was very well lit from the street lights. Why, according to you, did they use flashlights? Was it because the visibility was not very good? Why was it that somebody wanted to point a flashlight at you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: You know very well what I'm talking about. There was some lighting. However, there were no lights in the house where we were kept. So they wanted to see those who were jumping out of the window so that Milan Lukic could shoot them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Madam, may I remind you to pause before you give your answer. You came straight in then, and it was very hard for the interpreters to keep up with you. We want to hear what you say, but we'll lose it if you don't give us that pause. Yes, Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. I got a little upset.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We can understand that, madam, but we are just trying to make sure we get all of your evidence into the transcript. We understand that you are very involved in all of this, but we do ask you to keep in mind the need to pause before your answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have attempted through my questions and some quotes to obtain -- to elicit an answer from the witness concerning this prior statement that she gave and which I considered to be very significant. And in view of the responses that I received, regardless of the position that we should try with the Prosecutor to find an agreement, the number of discrepancies is such that I think it would be in the interest of justice for this statement to be admitted into evidence. I should like you to accept the possibility of the witness identifying her signature on the statement, and I would like to tender the statement into evidence as a Defence exhibit in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You may certainly ask her that question, and then we'll worry about whether it goes in as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have both the B/C/S and the English version of the statement given to the investigator.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, have you asked her? I have not heard you. Have you asked her whether that's her signature?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness has the statement in front of her.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And, madam, I would like you to have a look at the statement and confirm whether this is your signature on the statement which is in front of you. Have you had a look at the statement, madam?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Is that your statement, the one that you gave to the investigator in 1998?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender the statement into evidence as a Defence exhibit. Number D4, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution would object. I believe Mr. Domazet has had ample opportunity to cross-examine the witness regarding the contents of this statement. If the Court is inclined to accept this into evidence -- this witness has made three prior statements. I think in the interest of fairness to this witness, all three should be before the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: When you say he has had ample opportunity to cross-examine the witness, it may be because of the nature of the questions asked, to which I've already drawn attention that they were ambiguous, but he has attempted to obtain her assent to whether or not she had mentioned things in the statements -- through her statement, which she said yes. Now, the fact that they are not in this statement may not be an answer to it if she has given other statements. If she has mentioned them in other statements, then you would be entitled to get the other statements into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In that case, I would withdraw my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well. It will be Exhibit D4. Have we got a date of it? It's 12th and 13th of February, 1998. That is Exhibit D4. You understand, though, Mr. Domazet, that will probably make admissible any other statements she has made where she has mentioned these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I have no problem with that, with any other statement given by the witness to be tendered. May I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Madam, did you ever give a statement to the MUP, to the authorities of Bosnia and Herzegovina, any official statement concerning these events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember when that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Well, I was still in hospital when the doctors asked me about what I had gone through, because of the shape I was in. And I told them what had happened to me. Then some journalists came, and I told them my story.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You told your story to journalists, or to official authorities of the police, or some other state body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Both to the journalists and to the MUP officials, to whom I also gave a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So there's probably a statement of yours in the MUP in Gorazde, because it was at the time you were in hospital in Gorazde. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: As regards the interview, was it an interview that you gave to the Sarajevo television in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes, I also gave an interview in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Madam, do you remember that day in Pionirska Street? Did you see -- witness, have a look at your list VG78 and VG101. Did you see them on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: These people were not with us in Pionirska Street, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you say, madam, that they were not with you, does it mean that they were not in the Memic house while you were still there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, madam. This concludes my examination of the witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Witness 13, I want to draw your attention back to the point in time when you testified on cross-examination about Mr. Vasiljevic approaching (redacted) with a glass of brandy. Do you recall your testimony on that matter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately how long was Mr. Vasiljevic -- were Mr. Vasiljevic and (redacted) together at the time that you saw Mr. Vasiljevic with the glass of brandy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: It all happened in passing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you approximate in minutes how long it took?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: Three or four minutes altogether. "Hello. Hello. Here's something for you to drink." And they left.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that the following document be marked as Prosecution Document 59.1 and that a copy be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Are you going to introduce this in some way to us?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The English is at the back of it, Your Honour. 59.1 is the Bosnian version, B/C/S version, and 59.2 is the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: How does this arise out of cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's been numerous questions and even the introduction of a statement regarding what this witness did not say. This is a prior statement of the witness taken -- the first statement taken after the events of the 14th of June, and we will be seeking to introduce it as a prior consistent statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, if you can establish that. It doesn't appear to be so on its face, but you go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Witness 13, I would ask you to take a look at Prosecution Document Number 59.1 and refer you to the third page which says the number "114" on the bottom. I'd ask you to read that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG13
utterances.text: You want me to read it aloud or --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No. If you read it to yourself, please. And in particular, I would refer you to page 115, the second-from-the-last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You see, this is the very sort of problem that I can foresee here, Mr. Groome. You are entitled to get into evidence statements that she has made where she's referred to the matters which she's alleged not to have included within Exhibit D4. It may be that there is something here, but a quick read through doesn't suggest it. It certainly demonstrates that she has blamed Mr. Vasiljevic as a perpetrator for the fire, but that's not what she is being cross-examined about here. She's being cross-examined about three or four, and maybe more, specific matters that she's referred to in her evidence which were not in Exhibit D.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You can't have sort of a blunderbuss approach to this in re-examination. You are entitled to show that the three or four or more matters that she is alleged not to have included within Exhibit D and which from everything you've demonstrated so far she did not include within Exhibit D, that she has included in some other prior statement to meet an allegation of recent invention. That's what this is all about.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, now this statement, unless it has something in it which demonstrates she has, on a prior occasion, made a statement in which she's included one of those three or four matters, this is irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I know that the Court has just been presented with this, and it's a little difficult to understand at first glance, but if you look throughout the beginning of the statement, the witness is referring to "they," "they," "they," and mentions some of the incidents which counsel is now saying she omitted in this previous statement. The last paragraph of the statement, she refers to or identified who they are, and one of those people is Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, that does not impress me in the slightest, frankly, I have to say. We will need to go through the particular matters that she was alleged not to have referred to. But I mean there's matters of timing, for example, as to whether Mr. Vasiljevic was there when the men were sent off to bury the dead people and whether he was there at the time that they were moved from one house to the other. Now, I don't see any reference to any of that here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If I could just refer the Court to the first paragraph in the statement, it says: "They moved us over to the house of Adem Omeragic."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, but who are "they"?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The point, Your Honour, would be on the last paragraph, she identifies who they are, and Mitar Vasiljevic is one of those people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It depends what she means by "perpetrators." If she means being involved in the fire, she's clearly made that statement in Exhibit D.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I would just ask that I be permitted to ask the witness to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, that's hardly presenting a prior consistent statement if it has to be interpreted. You can have a go, Mr. Groome, but it just doesn't seem to me to get within anywhere near to what you are entitled to do in re-examination. But you give it a go and see how you go. But an interpretation by her now doesn't seem to carry very much weight as to what was intended in this document, if this was in fact her document, which isn't clear on the face of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and I recognise that the ultimate interpretation of the value of this is going to be for the Chamber to decide.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, it's got to have some value before it becomes admissible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Witness 13 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Wait a minute. Mr. Domazet is on his feet. Yes, Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I arose immediately, because as far as I understand, Mr. Groome would like to tender this as part of his redirect information by stating that this was the particular piece of information which was given by this witness. But this is not something that we can see from this statement. Moreover, I don't see this witness as being identified as the person who gave the statement. Quite the contrary. Three other individuals, who are not here today, are mentioned. Nowhere in this statement, at the beginning, at the heading, nor at the end of the statement, is it stated that this is what this particular witness said. I don't think that this can be the subject of additional examination. The statement was signed by some official in charge of the gathering of information, and then we have a name, and that is not this witness. So I don't think this can be tendered into evidence as an exhibit, nor can it be the basis -- the foundation for additional examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: If you had been listening, Mr. Domazet, you would have heard me say exactly that myself. Where is it her document?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if someone were to read the transcript of this Tribunal, her name would appear nowhere in it. It may be a very reasonable measure that was taken to protect the identity of the very few survivors of this. I just believe that the Prosecution is entitled to inquire in this area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: No, no. Look, Mr. Groome, where is there any indication that she was a party to this document at all?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: This was provided to Defence counsel in discovery as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Please, you just answer my question. Where does this Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. document demonstrate that she had played any part in it at all?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the content of the document is clear that it's her or it may be her. Her name does not appear on this document. I will admit that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Are you going to suggest that she was the only participant in this document? Because otherwise you cannot ascribe any particular part of it to her.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe I'm entitled to ask her -- she's already testified on cross-examination that she has given a statement to the MUP in this matter. I believe I'm entitled to ask her: Does she recognise this as that statement? She may very well say, no, she doesn't. If she does, then I'll sit down. But both Defence counsel and myself have always operated on the assumption or belief that this was a prior statement of hers, and it was provided in discovery as such.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: So that the reference to "I" means that it is a statement taken by the MUP, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I feel uncomfortable being put in a position of interpreting what the word "I" means. There are other facts within this statement; for example, the reference to the 13-year-old son. We heard from the son yesterday and this morning, who describes his age for the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Please, don't try and interpret it yourself. I want to know what you know. I know we don't have a jury, so we don't have a concern about, in the end, just rejecting it, but I don't want this to proceed on some form of guesswork, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I think the best way to eliminate guesswork is to ask the witness what she knows about this document that's before her now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, let's deal with that in the morning. But I think what you're going to have to do is to go through some care in the cross-examination, make out those parts of it where Mr. Domazet has suggested - and there has been no response to the contrary from you - that there were various statements she has made in her evidence here that were not in the statement which she gave which is now Exhibit D. Now, those are the only matters that you are entitled to raise in re-examination. Otherwise, it's not re-examination; it's something completely new.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And then you're going to have to work out where they are in this statement. And as I say, I have not yet myself seen any. Now, it may be that you've not had the opportunity of considering it, but I would prefer that you took some time and worked out where, in this statement, there is a reference to any of the matters that have been omitted from Exhibit D. And then, and then only, we're interested in whether this is her statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: They are the two points, and they are both equally important. So may I suggest you do that overnight, and then if this is her document and it does deal with those matters, not just in a global sense like in the last paragraph or second-to-last paragraph, then it would become admissible in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'll do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All right. Then we'll just leave it for the moment, and we'll resume again at 9.30 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
